Shape the stone piers with upstream noses and carry the timber deck onto clear gravel bank landings at z ±7, preserving the roughly 4 m width and 1 m water clearance. / Make it a pony-truss iron bridge. Run two side girders along z on each deck edge, each with a top chord (box 0.25×0.25, #263f40) at 1.9 m and a bottom chord at 1.0 m, joined by X-lattice diagonals (0.14×0.14 boxes at ±0.75 rad) every 1.4 m and with brass rivet dots on the top chord. Keep everything inside |x|,|z| ≤ 7. / Replace the white streaks with 5-6 short, irregular ripple shapes in #83b6bd and fade them. World rule: centrepiece: raise the target height to about 3-3.2 m with a finial so the town's heart out-silhouettes the tram stop and lamps.
elements.fix: Replace it with a Victorian cast-iron civic clock tower. Base: a sandstone plinth (box 2.4×0.6×2.4, #d3c7aa) on a 4.5 m round flagstone step (#918a7c, 0.18). problems: The end frames are plain dark rectangles and the slats are one orange block. It reads as the modern 'Timber-and-Aluminium Park Bench' in a different colour.
There is no curved back profile or armrest scroll to say cast-iron Victorian.
elements.fix: Make each cast-iron end a recognisable profile from 3 boxes: a back leg angled 0.25 rad, a front leg with a splayed foot (0.12×0.1×0.35), and an S-curved arm (two short boxes at ±0.4 rad) ending in a scroll knob (sphere 0.12). Split the seat into 3 slats and the back into 2 slats with visible 0.05 gaps (#8b6245 and #a67c54 alternating). Tilt the back 0.2 rad. Keep 14 parts.

problems: The front marker is a 1 m dark ring with a cream face and dots on a post. From the camera it looks like a ship's wheel or clock, has the same silhouette as the free-lot ring, and does not say 'build something for everyone here'.
The four brick-and-sandstone corner plinths are 0.4 m and read as small stray blocks on the gravel.
The layout matches the modern 'Community Town Lot' (corner blocks plus a sign by the front) recoloured.
The marker is a 0.98 m dark-and-cream disc on a 1.4 m post; at stream scale it is the same 'white dot on a stick' as the free-lot marker
The four corner plinths are fine, but the parcel has nothing saying 'for everyone'; it reads as an empty gravel lot

World rule: lotMarkers: the free-lot ring plate and the community-lot medallion are both round discs on a single post, and the free lot copies the modern sign's shape. Mandate distinct silhouettes. Free lot: a two-legged auctioneer/builder's board with the ochre empty ring, plus ochre-tipped surveyor's pegs at the four corners. Community lot: brick corner piers 0.8 m, a sandstone front kerb with a gap, and a green municipal notice frame with the civic emblem.

World rule: lotMarkers: the free-lot plate and the community-lot medallion are both specified as cream discs on posts, so they read the same. Specify distinct silhouettes: free lot = wide two-post cream enamel board with an ochre ring at about 2.2 m; community lot = civic-green twin-post noticeboard with a brass medallion, plus a front rope between the plinths.
elements.fix: Make the community lot read as municipal works ground. Raise the corner piers to 0.8 m brick (#a26048) with sandstone caps and a small green-painted iron ball finial. Run a low sandstone kerb line (0.15 high) along the front edge between the front piers, with a 2 m gap in the middle. Replace the disc-on-post with a municipal notice frame: a dark-green (#263f40) cast-iron frame on two short legs, a 1.6×1.0 cream panel, and the four-nodes-around-a-disc civic emblem large in green. Add a builder's handcart or a neat stack of bricks and timber in one back corner to signal 'to be built'. / Make the community marker a distinct silhouette: a 2.4 m twin-post municipal noticeboard painted civic green #596f52 with a 1.6 m brass-rimmed medallion. Run a low chain or rope between the four plinths along the front edge, and add a small stack of building materials (bricks, timber) in one corner to signal 'project ground'.

problems: The cream coat is near-white and stops at the hips, so the baron reads as a doctor or chef in a white jacket, not a travelling railway magnate.
The rolled concession map is not visible. The trunk carries the 'from far away' meaning on its own.
A 2.6x2.4 m brown-grey #928878 ground mat travels with the figure and shows as a dark rectangle on the square in the vignette
The cream coat on a cream body reads as a chef's or doctor's white coat, not a travelling railway baron
The rolled concession map is a small white stub; the trunk crest is too small to read
World rule: people/leader: specify the railway baron's coat as camel/tan and knee-length. A 'cream' coat cut at the hips renders as a white lab coat.

World rule: people/head/leader: add the rule 'figures stand directly at y 0 with no ground mat, plinth or base tile; the board and game supply the ground'. All three r1 figures carried flagstone or gravel mats that show in the vignette.
elements.fix: Recolour the coat to camel #c2a26e and extend it into a knee-length travel coat (box 0.5×0.55×0.3 below the hips, slightly flared) with a dark collar. Add brown gaiters over the boots, a gold watch chain across a dark waistcoat, and a clearly held 0.6 m rolled map (cylinder, #f2e7cb with a red ribbon) in the free hand. Put a bold red-and-brass railway crest on the trunk. / Delete the ground mat. Make the coat a knee-length camel #b8914e travelling ulster with a short dark shoulder cape and dark lapels. Make the map a 0.7 m roll held diagonally with a visible red rail line. Make the trunk 0.6 m with brass corners and a bold cream oval crest label.

problems: The right-hand facade is a full grid of dark glass panels: a glass curtain wall, which is anachronistic for the 1880s and the same reading as the modern 'Garden Steps Tower'.
Each setback is capped with a dark overhanging slab, which gives a pagoda or modern stacked-box silhouette rather than masonry cornices.
The right (side) facade is a full dark-framed blue glass grid that reads as a modern curtain wall, clashing with the brick-pier front
The rooftop brass bar is a small yellow line that doesn't read as the 'Brass Crown'

World rule: designDirection: give the builds concrete anti-recolour guidance. Café = two-storey terrace tea room with a timber shopfront (pilasters, fascia, stall riser, canvas roller blind), not a single-storey pavilion with white tables. Skyscraper = masonry piers and windows on every face, stone cornices, no glass curtain wall. Car = horse at true scale (about 1.6 m withers) with two shafts and a coachman's box. Dog = collar only, no saddles or vests.
World rule: designDirection/skyscraper: 'no glass curtain walls; every facade uses brick piers with sash windows'.
elements.fix: Give every face the same masonry treatment: brick piers (#a26048) every 1.2 m with separate tall windows (0.9×1.5, #83b6bd) on sandstone sills, and sandstone string courses at each floor. Replace the dark eave slabs at the setbacks with projecting sandstone cornices (0.3 deep, #d3c7aa). Give the ground floor a rusticated sandstone arcade of 3 round-headed openings. Crown it with a copper-green mansard or a heavy cornice plus a flagpole. / Rebuild the side facade like the front: red-brick piers between tall sash windows with stone sill bands at each setback. Replace the rooftop bar with a 1.2 m brass cupola or crown-shaped parapet (4 small brass finials) and a flagpole.

problems: The hound wears a teal-and-brown 'Victorian leather riding saddle' on its back. It is absurd on a dog and reads as the modern dog's harness vest recoloured.
Otherwise a decent chunky hound.

World rule: designDirection: add scale anchors for the examples. A dog has a back height of about 0.5 m and is under knee-to-hip height of a 1.8 m person, with no saddle. A cab horse has its withers at about 1.6 m and a body about 2.1 m long.
elements.fix: Delete the saddle and blanket parts. Keep a broad brown leather collar with brass studs and a brass tag (sphere 0.1). Optionally add a short rope lead trailing on the ground. Give the coat 1–2 white patches (chest, muzzle) so it reads as a working terrier or hound, not a recoloured beagle. / Scale the whole dog to about 0.45x: back about 0.5 m, head top about 0.7 m, length about 0.95 m. Delete the saddlecloth, saddle and strap parts. Keep only a thick brass collar (0.08 tall, #c89c42) with a round tag. Keep the beagle colouring and lengthen the ears to droop past the jaw.
